summary: Describes NIC user directories at SRI-ARC. It relates to RFCs 620 and 609 about the move of NIC services.

plainLanguage.summary: It explains the folders where NIC users keep files, as part of moving the service.

questions: nic user directories sri arc deletion
subtitle: Warning about deletion of NIC user directories during the move to OFFICE-1

tldr.problem: As the NIC moved from SRI-ARC to OFFICE-1, user directories at the old location needed to be removed and users needed to collect their data first.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 621 notifies users that all directories at SRI-ARC belonging to transferred NIC users will be deleted on Friday evening, March 8, 1974, and warns them to read any network mail stored there before that time.
tldr.outcome: Users had to migrate their data and email from the old location to the new facility at OFFICE-1.

today: RFC 621 documents a routine but critical administrative notification during the NIC relocation. It reflects the early ARPANET's need to coordinate infrastructure changes among all participating sites.

sections.title: User Directory Cleanup
sections.content:
RFC 621 announces that NIC user directories at SRI-ARC would be deleted on Friday evening, March 8, 1974, as part of the NIC's relocation to OFFICE-1. Any users who had been transferred to the new facility needed to retrieve their files and email before this deadline.

This action was coordinated with the hostname changes described in RFC 620, ensuring that after the cutover, the NIC name would point to OFFICE-1 exclusively.
sections.plainLanguage: The old NIC computers would delete all the user folders when people moved to the new building.

sections.title: Email Delivery Change
sections.content:
The timing of the directory deletion was critical for email delivery. After the change, network mail sent to a user at 'NIC' would go to OFFICE-1. However, mail sent to a user at 'SRI-ARC' after March 8 would fail to deliver, since that user's account no longer existed there.

Users had to ensure they received all pending network mail at SRI-ARC before the deletion, as nothing stored in the old system would be preserved.
sections.plainLanguage: After the move, mail sent to 'NIC' would reach you, but mail sent to 'SRI-ARC' would bounce because you weren't there anymore.

sections.title: User Responsibility
sections.content: RFC 621 emphasized that it was each user's responsibility to read and save any network mail delivered at SRI-ARC prior to the Friday evening deletion. This was a explicit acknowledgment that the cleanup was final and unrecoverable.
sections.plainLanguage: Everyone had to make sure they grabbed their email before it got thrown away forever.

references.text: Ferguson, B., "Request for Monitor Host Table Updates", RFC 620, March 1974.
